tasks.title: Checkpoint replacement ignores durability failures
tasks.discovered-by: Discovery-only static source inspection at pinned revision
tasks.evidence-before: writeCheckpoint ignores fallback fsync result at 359; ignores directory open failure and directory fsync result at 367–371, then returns success. A failed data barrier does not prevent rename of the replacement.
tasks.acceptance-criteria: Inject file and directory sync errors; preserve old journal before successful data sync; report uncertain durability after rename. Verify replay and crash recovery.

manual.problem_description: FileJournal.writeCheckpoint writes a replacement then calls F_FULLFSYNC; if it fails the fallback fsync result is ignored (line 359). It then renames over the original journal, attempts to open and sync the parent directory, ignores failure and returns success (367–372). A failed replacement-data barrier must not be followed by replacement of the only durable original. A directory sync failure after rename has different semantics: replacement may be visible but durability uncertain. Existing code conflates these states. Data loss is conditional on I/O failure/crash; no runtime reproduction yet.
proposed_solution: Read Journal.swift end-to-end, JournalError/JournalTypes, callers of compact/shutDown and existing JournalTests. Identify exact commit point (rename) and descriptor ownership. Coordinate design with 0011–0014, 0015 and 0029; keep focused task scope.

Introduce a small injectable syscall/filesystem interface or equivalent deterministic test seam for data sync, directory open/sync, rename, close and cleanup. Production default must call real syscalls. Capture errno immediately; do not use broad catch/try? to hide durability errors.

Use the existing strong Darwin barrier with checked fallback where supported. If both fail before rename, close and clean temporary file, return typed failure, keep original bytes/inode and append descriptor usable. Do not rename failed temp. If directory open/sync fails after rename, return explicit post-commit/uncertain-durability outcome; do not pretend rollback happened or blindly delete the new checkpoint.

Ensure compact reconciles descriptor with visible inode even when post-rename directory barrier failed; no later append should target an unlinked old inode. Preserve sidecar lock, O_NOFOLLOW and permissions. Decide whether directory sync unsupported is a separately documented policy, not unconditional success.
Propagate result through ContinuityCore/TinyTitanMemory callers and diagnostics. Add linked tasks for contract changes in every consumer; do not expose raw journal data in logs.

tasks.title: Prevent actor reentrancy from clearing unsynced append accounting
tasks.discovered-by: Discovery-only static source inspection at pinned revision
tasks.evidence-before: performBarrier awaits a blocking queue then sets pendingSinceSync to zero if descriptor unchanged. Actor can accept append while suspended; those records may be written after barrier syscall but before completion. Comment claiming appends queue behind the await is not a Swift actor guarantee.
tasks.acceptance-criteria: Deterministic barrier/append interleaving test; count only records captured by completed durability barrier, preserve newer pending writes.

manual.problem_description: performBarrier captures a descriptor, awaits a blocking queue, and then sets pendingSinceSync=0 if descriptor number is unchanged. Actor methods can be reentrant at await: a later append may occur after the actual flush but before completion resumes on the actor. That write is not necessarily durable yet can be cleared from accounting, potentially preventing a future flush. Descriptor equality is also not a generation identity if descriptors are reused. Existing comment that appends queue behind a suspended actor is not an enforceable guarantee.
proposed_solution: Map append(single/batch), afterAppend, sync, performBarrier, settleBarrier, compact, truncate and shutdown. Determine actual ordering and concurrent callers; pair design with 0012 and 0013.

Replace reset-all bookkeeping with monotonic append and durable generations or a captured pending watermark. Capture watermark and stable descriptor generation before dispatch; a successful barrier advances durable watermark only to the captured point. Later writes remain pending even if the OS happened to flush them.

Serialize barrier operations or coalesce with explicitly owned in-flight state; distinguish task cancellation from syscall completion. Keep descriptor lifetime valid until syscall ends; use generation identity not only numeric fd. Ensure newer writes schedule a further barrier and max latency cannot be postponed.

Use actor-owned state or existing synchronization primitives; avoid @unchecked Sendable additions or blocking cooperative executor. Handle counters/overflow with deliberate strategy and preserve single/batch semantics and error propagation.
verification_steps: Build a deterministic controllable barrier seam: append A, start barrier, signal actual flush completion but hold actor continuation, append B, then resume A barrier. Assert B still pending and a subsequent barrier clears it. Original code should fail the assertion.

Test overlapping sync requests, batch sizes, failed barrier retaining pending state, cancellation, descriptor replacement and generation rollover boundary if applicable. Avoid sleep-based synchronization; use explicit continuations/latches.

Retain tests `theBarrierLandsOnceAppendsStop`, `aBusyWriterCannotPostponeDurabilityForever`, `explicitSyncIsImmediate` and `compactionWaitsForAnInFlightBarrier`. Run `swift test --no-parallel --filter JournalTests`, full suite, lint and `swift test --no-parallel --sanitize=thread`.
Verify public diagnostics count is exact at each controlled ordering and no flush task leaks. Compare warnings and latency/behavior with baseline; no numerical/model change needed.
self_audit_steps: Cold-read every suspension point; prove invariant durableGeneration <= appendedGeneration and pending equals difference. Check replacement/close cannot race in-flight barrier.
Review test scheduling independence; test must fail on old code for the targeted interleaving, not pass probabilistically.
Ensure 0012 remains independently tested for actual append preservation across rename.

tasks.title: Establish serialization of append versus compaction
tasks.discovered-by: Discovery-only static source inspection at pinned revision
tasks.evidence-before: compact awaits a checkpoint replacement on a blocking queue; append writes to existing descriptor. Unless every caller provides external serialization, an append during suspension may land on the old inode and disappear after reopen. Caller contract not yet established.
tasks.acceptance-criteria: Trace all FileJournal callers; reproduce with controlled suspension; guarantee append preservation or explicitly enforce isolation.
tasks.classification: investigation candidate; not a confirmed defect

manual.problem_description: Investigation, not a confirmed reachable production defect. compact awaits settleBarrier and then async replacement; append is independently actor-callable and writes current descriptor. If append runs during replacement or between snapshot capture and reopening, it may be written to old inode and lost when checkpoint replaces path. External serialization could prohibit this; trace every caller before fixing. A snapshot taken before compaction admission can itself be stale even if I/O is serialized.
proposed_solution: Trace FileJournal compact/append callers in ContinuityCore and TinyTitanMemory, including tasks, public protocols, tests and direct API use. Document exactly which actor/lock owns the logical snapshot and journal ordering, and whether caller suspension allows concurrent calls.

Build a deterministic compact seam that pauses before rename and before descriptor reopen. If reachable, classify actual data-loss path S0 and record a severity update, not a new duplicate task. If not reachable, document the enforced invariant and add regression coverage; don't invent a fix.

Prefer one explicit serialization contract for append/compact/truncate/shutdown, with nonblocking async admission and safe cancellation. Serialize snapshot capture with mutation or checkpoint watermark; either queue append until replacement is installed or replay a proven delta onto new journal. Do not hold locks across await or block executor.

Preserve ordering and sidecar lock, ensure no accepted append is dropped or duplicated, including when compaction fails pre/post rename or reopening fails. Link consumer changes if API contract changes. Avoid a fake success that skips compaction.
verification_steps: Regression: append A, request checkpoint at known state, pause replacement, concurrently append B; resume, close/reopen and assert durable state contains A and B exactly once in intended order. Also test append while snapshot is being captured, batch append, competing compactions and shutdown.
Inject compaction pre-rename and post-rename failure; verify queued operations resolve correctly and no deadlock/old inode write. Prove no descriptor use-after-close under TSan.

If no defect exists due to caller contract, add a positive deterministic test proving enforced isolation and public API cannot bypass it; include all call sites in evidence. No speculative source change required.
Run JournalTests, memory/continuity integration, full suite and TSan; verify warnings and coverage unchanged or improved.
self_audit_steps: Read caller and callee together; distinguish actor isolation from serialization across suspension. Check snapshot watermark and append admission under every failure path.
Verify exact-once replay assertions, no time.sleep, no disabled test and no unbounded waiting.
Record proof of non-reachability or actual reproduced/fixed behavior; never mark DONE based only on a lock comment.

tasks.title: Propagate asynchronous journal durability failures
tasks.discovered-by: Discovery-only static source inspection at pinned revision
tasks.evidence-before: Scheduled performBarrier uses try?; shutDown also discards errors from settleBarrier and performBarrier before closing and releasing lock, despite async throws signature.
tasks.acceptance-criteria: Fault inject fsync errors; expose degraded status and shutdown error while guaranteeing resource cleanup; verify retry and pending count.

manual.problem_description: Scheduled background barrier uses `try? await self.performBarrier()`; shutDown declared async throws also suppresses settleBarrier and performBarrier errors before closing descriptors. A storage failure can leave caller unaware, pending records unsynced, and shutdown apparently successful. Cancellation during sleep is expected and should be distinguished from I/O failure; do not report every normal cancellation as corruption.
proposed_solution: Trace diagnostics/degraded-state APIs and consumers of FileJournal sync/shutDown, including memory service shutdown. Define typed error or state for background durability failure, recovery and shutdown failure.

Change background task handling to explicitly catch cancellation only where intended, capture actual I/O failure in actor-owned observable state, preserve pending watermark and use bounded retry policy or surface failure until caller retries. No infinite retry or silent catch.

Ensure `shutDown` attempts flush, always releases resources in correct order even on error, and returns the original meaningful durability failure. If flush succeeds after an earlier background failure, define whether diagnostic remains recorded and when degraded state clears.

Use same barrier and descriptor lifetime policy as 0010/0011/0012. Update every affected caller to propagate/log safe error category and not claim persistence when failed. Avoid logging record contents.
verification_steps: Inject persistent barrier failure and assert background failure becomes visible without dropping pending records; subsequent successful explicit sync clears pending with documented diagnostic behavior.

Test cancellation of scheduled sleep (no false failure), shutdown flush failure (throws, lock released, descriptors closed), successful shutdown/reopen and repeat shutdown according to contract. Ensure caller reports degraded memory or failure rather than normal success.
Add tests in JournalTests and relevant TinyTitanMemory failure suites; run targeted tests, full suite, TSan and lint on Mac A.
Compare baseline failures and warnings; no swallowed I/O error remains on touched path.
self_audit_steps: Trace error from syscall to public caller, including fallback, cancellation and cleanup. Verify cleanup cannot overwrite original error or falsely clear state.
Cold-read retries, scheduled task ownership and shutdown admission; ensure no retry loop continues after close.
Check logs contain no record contents or credentials and negative tests fail before fix.

tasks.title: Distinguish corrupt complete journal records from torn tail
tasks.discovered-by: Discovery-only static source inspection at pinned revision
tasks.evidence-before: decodeRecords silently drops every complete line whose JSON decoding fails, not just a final unterminated tail; no diagnostic is returned. Corruption or incompatible records may be lost before compaction.
tasks.acceptance-criteria: Test middle-line corruption and incompatible records; report rejected record positions, preserve recoverability and avoid destructive compaction without policy.

manual.problem_description: decodeRecords splits newline-delimited JSON and uses try? to silently drop every undecodable complete line. A torn unterminated last line is legitimately recoverable; an invalid complete middle record, incompatible version, or corrupt checkpoint is different. Returning a successful partial replay can cause later compaction to overwrite recoverable original bytes. Need preserve availability when appropriate, but not treat corruption as empty or successful replay.
proposed_solution: Read JournalRecord schema, FileJournal replay/read, tail recovery and caller compaction behavior. Decide compatibility policy: supported schema migration vs unsupported record vs malformed data vs unterminated tail. Do not silently narrow existing format support.

Introduce a replay result or typed error with safe record location/line, failure class, and recovered valid records if necessary. Avoid storing/printing raw memory contents. Preserve last unterminated tail recovery semantics; treat complete invalid records explicitly.

Require callers to avoid destructive compaction/checkpoint replacement when replay integrity is uncertain unless there is an explicit operator-approved recovery procedure. Preserve original file or use a safe read-only/degraded path, not live migration.

If API shape changes, enumerate FileJournal.read/replay consumers, ContinuityCore, memory CLI and tests; add linked contract tasks for all consumers. Prefer backward compatibility where semantics can remain correct.
verification_steps: Add fixtures: valid lines before/after malformed complete middle line, invalid complete final line, unsupported record version, corrupt checkpoint, blank line, valid final newline and torn unterminated tail. Assert exact diagnostic and correct recovery policy; old code silently succeeds on complete corruption.
Verify a failed/degraded replay cannot trigger destructive compaction; compare original file bytes and ensure no records silently lost. Test read-only inspection and normal replay ordering.

Retain `aTornTailIsDroppedAndTheRestSurvives`, `anUnterminatedFinalLineIsDropped`, `anUnterminatedTailDoesNotCostTheRecordAfterIt`; do not weaken them. Run JournalTests, memory integration/full suite and lint.
Test any version compatibility path with historical synthetic fixture and document supported behavior; no production data migration.
self_audit_steps: Cold-read decoder and all consumers; ensure explicit error vs recovery states distinguish absent file, corrupt file and torn tail.
Inspect tests for exact preserved bytes and no use of try? that hides corruption. Review handling of untrusted record sizes if touched; record separate task for bounds gaps.
Verify no recovery logic leaks data or changes live journals.

tasks.title: Validate journal file type, ownership and permissions

Assert refusal or documented allowed behavior before side effects.
Verify read-only path cannot follow disallowed link or block on FIFO; compare sentinel file bytes and permissions; no actual sensitive file used.
Retain journal ownership and lock tests; test race-sensitive operations via descriptor checks, not sleeps. Run JournalTests, memory suite, lint/SAST and TSan as applicable.

Confirm threat model and tests support severity/closure decision.

tasks.title: Handle short pread during tail repair without truncating unread bytes
tasks.discovered-by: Discovery-only static source inspection at pinned revision
tasks.evidence-before: Tail repair accepts any nonnegative read length, searches only the returned prefix, then sets end to offset, skipping an unread suffix if a short read occurs. Subsequent ftruncate may discard a complete record.
tasks.acceptance-criteria: Inject short reads and EINTR; require complete range reads or fail without truncating; verify byte-identical valid tail.

manual.problem_description: dropDanglingTail scans backward by a requested chunk size. `pread` may return fewer bytes than requested; code searches only buffer[0..<read] then moves end to the chunk offset. The unread suffix is skipped; if it contains the last newline, keep may be too small and ftruncate may remove valid records. Negative EINTR is treated as failure, which is safe but needlessly brittle; zero progress likewise needs explicit handling. Actual normal disk short-read frequency is unknown.
proposed_solution: Inspect FileJournal+Opening.swift and journal startup sequence. Preserve exclusive lock and same-descriptor scan/truncate invariant. Add a scoped read seam for fault injection.

Implement exact-range pread helper: loop while requested bytes remain, advancing pointer and offset by bytes actually read; retry EINTR, reject other errors, reject unexpected EOF/zero progress while scanning known fstat size. Use checked offsets/counts and maintain correct chunk boundaries.

Search a chunk only after all bytes are successfully read. If scan cannot prove the last complete newline, throw and leave original length untouched. Check ftruncate and preserve errno. Decide how to handle concurrent external modification under trust policy 0015.
Do not rewrite journal schema, drop complete records, or compensate by disabling tail recovery.
verification_steps: Add deterministic tests returning short positive read, EINTR then success, unexpected zero/EOF, and hard error. Place last newline in the previously skipped suffix across chunk boundary. Compare entire file before/after; failure paths preserve original bytes.
Test empty file, file ending newline, no newline, exact 64 KiB boundary, multi-chunk valid history and torn suffix. Verify only proven dangling bytes are removed.
Run JournalTests and full suite, lint, relevant sanitizer/TSan; ensure no new warning and no sleep synchronization.
Capture test failing on old algorithm for the short-read fixture.
self_audit_steps: Cold-read offset math and loop termination; verify no underflow/overflow, no uninitialized bytes searched and no ftruncate before complete scan.
Review test seam is production-default real pread and does not hide failures.
Check linked journal recovery semantics with 0014.

tasks.title: Bound HTTP header buffering before decoder completes
tasks.discovered-by: Discovery-only static source inspection at pinned revision
tasks.evidence-before: Source explicitly acknowledges NIO accumulates unbounded small headers before application aggregate-limit checks. Pipeline config has no earlier aggregate bound. Server binds loopback, limiting exposure but not local denial of service.
tasks.acceptance-criteria: Add pre-decode aggregate header byte/count gate or prove equivalent decoder protection; test incrementally supplied oversized headers and bounded RSS.

manual.problem_description: HTTPServer source explicitly states NIO accumulates an unbounded number of headers before handler sees the complete request head. The 16 KiB/128-field application cap and 64 connection cap therefore do not limit decoder buffering for a single incremental header stream. Idle deadline is activity-based; continuous small reads may postpone it. Loopback limits exposure, not local resource exhaustion. Confirm actual NIO version and pipeline behavior; avoid speculative blanket raw-byte cap that breaks bodies, pipelining or chunked requests.
proposed_solution: Inspect pinned SwiftNIO version and decoder APIs, HTTPServer pipeline and handler idle/connection caps. Trace header bytes before request-head emission and verify whether a supported decoder option solves aggregate limit.

Prefer a supported aggregate header byte/count limit at decoder layer. If unavailable, design a bounded HTTP framing guard that understands request boundaries and partial reads, or a verified parser configuration; do not duplicate HTTP incorrectly. Ensure initial line, CRLF boundaries, multiple headers, chunked bodies/trailers and pipelining remain valid. Consider absolute head deadline independent of activity, as linked task if needed.

Keep existing application 431 checks, connection cap, body cap and error behavior. If early rejection cannot safely produce 431, close deterministically and document behavior with tests; no unbounded buffering waiting for end-of-headers. Release resources on disconnect.
Keep loopback binding and no live endpoint test; measure memory using isolated server with synthetic backend.
verification_steps: Extend `tests/TinyTitanServer/HTTPServerTests.swift` (`anOversizedHeaderBlockIsRefused` and stalled body tests) with fragmented over-limit header bytes before terminal CRLF, aggregate field-count boundary, single long header and slow-but-active partial head. Assert deterministic bound/closure and no generation started.

Test valid headers at both limits, normal request body > header cap within body cap, SSE, pipelining, HEAD, keep-alive, malformed framing and chunked requests/trailers if supported. Preserve response ordering.

Use NIOEmbedded or controlled loopback fixture with synthetic backend; measure buffered bytes or RSS via repeatable instrumentation, not live load. Prove memory bounded as input increases; bounded timeout, no huge stress payload necessary.
Run HTTPServerTests, full package suite, TSan and lint; inspect actual decoder config and code scanner.
self_audit_steps: Cold-read framing state machine across fragmented/pipelined requests and error/close transitions; check counters reset only at correct boundary and no integer overflow.
Review tests prove pre-decode bound rather than only rejection after complete head. Confirm body/SSE and legitimate clients still work.
No dependency upgrade without explicit compatibility task, lock update and full regression verification.

tasks.title: Bound stored response memory by bytes and chain size
tasks.discovered-by: Discovery-only static source inspection at pinned revision
tasks.evidence-before: ResponseStore caps number of entries, not bytes; each continuation flattens prior conversation into storedInput, and entries retain input/output plus response JSON. A count cap does not bound accumulated history byte size. Generation context limits may reduce practical impact; measure.
tasks.acceptance-criteria: Test long continuation chains and many near-limit responses; enforce aggregate byte budget and chain bounds; document eviction semantics.

manual.problem_description: ResponseStore is globally count-bounded at default 256 entries but retains responseJSON, inputItems and outputItems, and previous_response_id copies flattened prior history into each new entry. Count-only cap permits large total retained memory and repeated history; model context validation may constrain some requests but does not prove a server-wide byte bound. Actual growth depends on storage sharing, request size and generated outputs. Existing item lookup also allocates combined arrays.
proposed_solution: Trace response creation, store=false, streaming/nonstreaming put, references, retrieval/delete and context validation. Measure entry memory representation and realistic worst-case retained bytes; document limits independent of model context. Identify any shared arrays/data and avoid claiming exact RSS from logical size alone.

Introduce explicit configurable or justified total byte/entry weight budget and per-entry/chain limit. Use checked arithmetic, account replacement/delete/eviction under existing lock or an appropriate actor, and prevent unbounded accumulation. Consider bounded structural sharing only if lookup/eviction semantics remain correct.

Define deterministic policy for oversize entry and prior references: reject or evict with documented API semantics; do not silently report a stored response that cannot be retrieved. Preserve store=false behavior, insertion order, replacement refresh and retrieval/input_items/cancel semantics.

Avoid expensive serialization under lock or repeated scans on hot path; consider measured logical byte accounting with conservative overhead. Update response handlers and tests as needed; don't change API without linked consumer verification.
verification_steps: Extend `tests/TinyTitanServer/ResponseStoreTests.swift` with mixed-sized entries, replacement larger/smaller, deletion, eviction by bytes and count, zero/invalid capacity, oversize single entry and arithmetic overflow boundaries. Assert total accounting never exceeds budget.

HTTP-level tests for repeated previous_response_id chain, long messages, streamed and non-streamed stored outputs, store=false, prior response eviction, GET/input_items and item_reference; verify documented error behavior and no silent truncation.
Measure retained logical bytes and RSS trend in isolated synthetic test, comparing baseline and fix. Avoid expecting RSS to drop immediately due to allocator caching.
Run ResponseStoreTests, API surface tests, full suite, lint and TSan; compare response protocol and warnings with baseline.
self_audit_steps: Cold-read lock invariants, count/weight updates on every mutation and no multiplication overflow; verify a rejected insertion cannot corrupt ordering/accounting.
Review tests prove aggregate limit under repeated chain and high-size entry, not only count cap. Confirm no hidden changes to generated text or model defaults.
Check public contract and any docs/clients are updated consistently.

tasks.title: Prove allocation products and BLAS narrowing safe at Swift–C boundary
tasks.discovered-by: Discovery-only static source inspection at pinned revision
tasks.evidence-before: Scratch sizes multiply size_t dimensions without overflow checks; BLAS dimensions explicitly narrow to int. C entry point checks only nonzero dimensions. Need caller reachability and shape bounds before classifying runtime impact.
tasks.acceptance-criteria: Trace all Swift callers and manifest-derived dimensions; test overflow/INT_MAX boundary in isolated sanitizer harness; reject unsafe geometry before allocating or narrowing.
tasks.classification: investigation candidate; not a confirmed defect

manual.problem_description: Investigation. `tinytitan_delta_rule_chunk` calculates 2*tokens and multiple size_t allocation products unchecked, then explicitly narrows tokens/dk/dv to int for BLAS. If caller geometry is unbounded, wraparound can underallocate and later memcpy/loop can write out of bounds; narrowing can yield invalid BLAS dimensions. If validated Swift shapes strictly bound all dimensions, runtime path may be safe today but C API contract still needs proof. The function's fallback returns 1 both when it produces sequential output and when dv is too large for fallback; caller interpretation also needs inspection.
proposed_solution: Locate every `tinytitan_delta_rule_chunk` declaration, caller, Swift wrapper and tests with `git grep -n`; trace geometry to model manifests/config and buffer lengths. Read all C function, header and BLAS wrapper, including allocation failure branch and strides. Record valid dimension/stride bounds and ownership.

If reachable, add checked `size_t` multiplication/addition helpers (strict C99 using SIZE_MAX checks), validate every allocation product and BLAS argument fits INT_MAX before cast. Check zero semantics, stride minima, total buffer span assumptions and error code contract. Reject before allocation/use; no compiler-extension or warning suppression.

Clarify distinction between success, fallback-produced output and no-output allocation failure; coordinate every caller and ensure no uninitialized readout or partially mutated state on error. If C API intentionally assumes checked Swift wrapper, prove and enforce wrapper preconditions and document header contract; add local checks where public misuse can occur.
Keep fast-path arithmetic and numerical ordering unchanged for valid dimensions; use existing performance/golden gates if any hot-path behavior changes. Do not allocate huge memory in tests.
verification_steps: Construct isolated C unit/harness inputs with tiny safe buffers and invalid dimensions rejected before dereference: SIZE_MAX product overflow, 2*tokens overflow, INT_MAX+1 BLAS dimension, bad strides, zero and valid boundary. Use fault-injection allocation failure on both fallback-valid and fallback-invalid dv.

Trace Swift return handling and regression test invalid manifest-derived geometry with controlled fixture, ensuring clean typed error not trap. Verify valid numerical output matches existing reference/golden tests.
